body:
124 rule files said deploying the rule "satisfies" an EU AI Act article (or a NIST, ISO or OWASP item). docs/COMPLIANCE-COVERAGE-POLICY.md allows only "provides detection evidence supporting ...". 135 lines now say "provides detection evidence supporting", "supports" or, for OWASP categories, "matches".

Only lines inside the top-level compliance block were touched. Two uses of "satisfy" that describe an attack (a forged origin that satisfies a localhost check, payloads that pre-satisfy an approval gate) are left as they are.

scripts/validate-compliance.ts gains check 4: a context that claims compliance ("satisfies the Article ...", "makes ... compliant", "ensures compliance") fails CI.

How this was checked:
- Parsed before and after, every field outside compliance is identical in all 124 files. The engine never reads compliance, so detection is unchanged and no rule_version moves.
- Inserting "satisfies the Article 15 requirement" into ATR-2026-02403 made validate:compliance fail; removing it passed.
- Local runs: validate, validate:compliance, audit:mappings --require-full, both crosswalk --check, check-rules-safety --base origin/main (124 modified, no new benign FPs, own TPs still match), gate:generalization.
title: fix(rules): mapping rationales say "supports", never "satisfies"
head: fix/mapping-wording
